items.title: Heegaard Floer plus and infinity groups and absolute grading for rational homology spheres
items.statement:
A rational homology sphere is a closed connected oriented three-manifold $Y$ with $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. Let $\mathfrak t$ be a Spin$^c$ structure on $Y$, meaning a principal $\mathrm{Spin}^c(3)$ lift of the oriented frame bundle. A pointed Heegaard diagram for $(Y,\mathfrak t)$ consists of a closed oriented surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_g)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_g)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves which bound complete disk systems in the two genus-$g$ handlebodies of a Heegaard splitting of $Y$, with every $\alpha_i$ transverse to every $\beta_j$, and a basepoint $z\in\Sigma\setminus(\boldsymbol\alpha\cup\boldsymbol\beta)$; the diagram is restricted to the generators assigned to $\mathfrak t$. Compactness of $\Sigma$ makes the transverse intersection set finite. A periodic domain is an integral two-chain in the complementary regions whose boundary is an integral sum of attaching curves. The diagram is strongly admissible for $\mathfrak t$ when every nonzero periodic domain $P$ with $n_z(P)=0$ and $\langle c_1(\mathfrak t),[P]\rangle\ge0$ has at least one positive and one negative region coefficient.

For such a diagram, put $\mathbb T_\alpha=\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_g$ and $\mathbb T_\beta=\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_g$ in $\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)=\Sigma^g/S_g$. A generator is an intersection point $\mathbf x\in\mathbb T_\alpha\cap\mathbb T_\beta$. A Whitney disk class $\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a relative homotopy class of disks in $\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)$ with boundary arcs on the two product tori and endpoints $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$; its Maslov index is $\mu(\phi)$ and its local multiplicity at $z$ is $n_z(\phi)$. For a regular almost-complex datum for which every relevant count is finite and the disk-count operator squares to zero, define $CF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)$ over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ on generators $[\mathbf x,i]$, $i\in\mathbb Z$, with differential
$$
\partial^\infty[\mathbf x,i]=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\\\mu(\phi)=1,\ n_z(\phi)\ge0}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)[\mathbf y,i-n_z(\phi)].
$$
Here $\mathbb F_2$ is the field with two elements, $U[\mathbf x,i]=[\mathbf x,i-1]$, and $\#_2$ is the finite count modulo two. The submodule generated by $[\mathbf x,i]$ with $i<0$ is $CF^-(Y,\mathfrak t)$, $CF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)=CF^\infty/CF^-$, and $HF^\infty$ and $HF^+$ denote their homology when the differential is established. Relative Maslov gradings are fixed by the Fredholm index and the shift under $U$ is $-2$.

When the standard absolute rational Maslov grading is available, normalize it so that the generator of $HF^\infty(S^3)$ has degree zero. For a smooth Spin$^c$ cobordism $(W,\mathfrak s)$ between rational homology spheres, the induced map is assigned degree shift
$$
\frac{\langle c_1(\mathfrak s)^2\rangle-2\chi(W)-3\sigma(W)}{4},
$$
where $c_1(\mathfrak s)$ is the first Chern class, $\chi(W)$ is Euler characteristic, $\sigma(W)$ is the signature, and its square is evaluated using the rational intersection form of $W$. This is a convention for a Floer package when constructed; it asserts neither existence of generic regular data nor that the disk-count differential squares to zero. Heegaard invariance, the absolute grading on general $(Y,\mathfrak t)$, and cobordism-map properties are separate claims.

items.title: Spin-c structures on a fixed oriented bundle form an H2 torsor
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $E\to X$ be an oriented real vector bundle over a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff compactly generated weak Hausdorff space of CW homotopy type, and suppose one numerable Spin$^c$ lift of its oriented frame bundle is given. Among numerable Spin$^c$ lifts of that same frame bundle, isomorphism classes form a torsor for $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$: tensoring a lift by a complex line bundle defines a free and transitive action, identified with $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$ by the first Chern class. For a continuous map $f:X\to Z$ between bases with these hypotheses and an oriented bundle $E_Z\to Z$, the pullback action on lifts of $f^*E_Z\to X$ is equivariant for $f^*:H^2(Z;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$.

items.title: Heegaard Floer correction term
items.statement: Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere, let $\mathfrak t$ be a Spin$^c$ structure, and suppose the Heegaard Floer groups, absolute rational grading, and natural map $\iota_*:HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)\to HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ are defined and independent of the construction choices. View $HF^+$ as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module. An element is $U$-torsion if some positive power of $U$ annihilates it. The correction term $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ is the minimum absolute grading of a nonzero homogeneous element in $\operatorname{im}\iota_*$. In the standard plus tower every element is $U$-torsion, although every element is divisible by every positive power of $U$; these two properties are compatible. The definition uses the nonzero homogeneous image elements, rather than imposing $U$-nontorsion. The standard normalization is $d(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)=0$ for the unique Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t_0$ on $S^3$. Existence of the minimum and independence of choices are separate proof obligations.

items.title: Spin-c extensions over a rational ball form a metabolizer coset
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $B$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$ and connected rational homology sphere boundary $Y$. The coefficient sequence $0\to\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\to0$ gives an isomorphism $\beta:H^1(Y;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. Define the cohomological linking pairing by
$$\lambda_Y(x,y)=\langle\beta^{-1}(x)\smile y,[Y]\rangle\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z.$$
Under Poincare duality $H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, this pairing agrees, up to the global orientation sign, with the chain torsion linking pairing: for torsion classes represented by oriented 1-cycles $C,D$, choose $n>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=nC$, and set $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/n\pmod{\mathbb Z}$. The two conventions therefore have the same annihilator subgroups.
Let $M$ be the image of restriction $H^2(B;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ and $M^\perp=\{x:\lambda_Y(m,x)=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$. Then the boundary Spin$^c$ structures extending over $B$ form one affine coset of $M$, the pairing is nonsingular, $M=M^\perp$, and $|M|^2=|H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)|$.

items.title: Heegaard invariance and well-definedness of the correction term
items.statement: For every closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere $Y$ and Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$, the standard Heegaard Floer groups $HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)$ and $HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ constructed from admissible pointed Heegaard diagrams are independent, up to grading-preserving isomorphism, of the diagram and regular auxiliary data. The image of $HF^\infty\to HF^+$ is a graded plus tower, isomorphic as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module to $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]/U\mathbb F_2[U]$ with an absolute rational grading shift and with $U$ of degree $-2$. Its nonzero homogeneous elements have a least grading, and that least grading is independent of the diagram and auxiliary data. Every tower element is $U$-torsion and is divisible by every power of $U$. In the standard normalization the least grading for $(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)$ is zero.

items.title: Correction-term inequality from a rational-ball cobordism map
items.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth compact connected oriented four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$ and oriented boundary the rational homology sphere $Y$, where $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. Let $\mathfrak t$ be a boundary Spin$^c$ structure extending over $B$. Removing an open four-ball from the interior gives a Spin$^c$ cobordism $W$ with boundary $-S^3\sqcup Y$, and each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism on rational homology. In both orientations, the induced Heegaard Floer infinity map is an isomorphism of degree zero and the corresponding plus-map inequality gives $d(Y,\mathfrak t)\ge0$ and $d(Y,\mathfrak t)\le0$.

items.title: Lens-space correction-term formula for L(p,1)
items.statement:
Use the Ozsvath–Szabo orientation convention $L(p,1)$ given by positive $p$-surgery on the unknot and label its Spin$^c$ structures by $i\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, represented by $0\le i<p$. For every integer $p\ge1$,
$$d(L(p,1),i)=\frac{(2i-p)^2-p}{4p}.$$
For the opposite orientation the correction terms are negated, with the conjugate Spin$^c$ label understood.

items.title: A rational homology ball bounded by L(4,1)
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $Q\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ be the nonsingular complex conic parametrized by $[s:t]\mapsto[s^2:st:t^2]$, let $N(Q)$ be a closed tubular disk bundle, and let $B_2=\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\operatorname{int}N(Q)}$. Then $B_2$ is a smooth compact four-manifold with $H_*(B_2;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$. Its boundary is the circle bundle of Euler number $4$ over $S^2$, hence is the lens space $L(4,1)$ up to orientation; orient $B_2$ so that the boundary agrees with the stated lens-space convention.

items.title: Correction terms vanish on extending Spin-c structures over rational homology balls
items.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth compact connected oriented four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$ and oriented boundary the rational homology sphere $Y$, where $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. If a boundary Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$ extends over $B$, then its Heegaard Floer correction term vanishes: $d(Y,\mathfrak t)=0$. The extension hypothesis is essential; no vanishing is asserted for Spin$^c$ structures that do not extend.

items.title: The smooth slice-disk double cover is a rational homology ball
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary $K$. Let $W_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$. Then $W_D$ is a rational homology four-ball and its oriented boundary is the double branched cover $\Sigma_2(K)$ formed using the positive-meridian convention. This assertion concerns smooth disks only and makes no claim for locally flat topological disks.

items.title: Double-cover correction terms obstruct smooth sliceness
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot admitting a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ (a smooth embedding of the closed disk with interior in $\operatorname{int}B^4$ and boundary $K\subset S^3$). Let $W_D$ be its connected double cover branched along $D$, so $H_*(W_D;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$, and let $Y=\Sigma_2(K)$ be the oriented double branched cover of $S^3$ using the positive-meridian convention. Then $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. Define the torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ on $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ by $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\cdot D)/n\pmod{\mathbb Z}$ when $\partial F=nC$, with signed intersection in the oriented $Y$. Under Poincare duality, the restriction image of $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W_D)$ in $\operatorname{Spin}^c(Y)$ is an affine coset of a subgroup $M\subseteq H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $M=M^\perp$, where $M^\perp=\{x:\lambda_Y(m,x)=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$; such a subgroup is a metabolizer. It has $|M|^2=|H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)|$. Every extending structure $\mathfrak t$ in this coset satisfies $d(Y,\mathfrak t)=0$. No conclusion is asserted for a merely locally flat topological disk (a topological embedding with local flat disk charts but no smoothness hypothesis) or for nonextending boundary structures.

items.title: A nonextendible Spin-c structure with nonzero d on a rational-ball boundary
items.statement: The false claim is: if a closed oriented three-manifold $Y$ with $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$ bounds a smooth compact four-manifold $B$ with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$, then a nonzero correction term $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ for any boundary Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$ obstructs the existence of $B$.
